meta.purpose: Every scripture quoted or referenced in Gideon's writings, fetched from named digital editions and verified word-for-word, banked so future work needs no repeat online confirmation.

editions.brenton: Brenton Septuagint (1851 English), eBible.org id eng-Brenton — OT only
editions.gnv: Geneva Bible 1599, eBible.org id enggnv — whole Bible
editions.kjv: King James Version 1769 standard text, eBible.org id eng-kjv2006 — whole Bible

conventions: status: confirmed = quote matches the cited edition word-for-word; confirmed-excerpt = word-for-word but partial (ellipsis/clipped); differs-minor = same verse, few words changed; paraphrase = reworded; anchor = referenced narratively, not quoted; commentary = article's own rendering (canonical texts banked for reference).

For HALLOWED BE THY NAME: quotes cited 'LXX, Brenton' verified against Brenton's English Septuagint; quotes cited 'Geneva' against the 1599 Geneva Bible. Uncited blockquotes diagnosed against KJV (their usual voice) with GNV/Brenton banked alongside.
Psalms: the article cites Hebrew-psalm numbers (Ps 22:16); Brenton prints LXX numbers (Ps 21:17). Both recorded.
Hebrew names in the body (Moshe, Yohoshua, Yerushalayim, etc.) are the author's intentional practice - never flagged.
Ben Yachid uses JPS 1917 (Tanakh) + Geneva (NT); add JPS entries to this bank when those verses next need verification.

sections.label: Part One — The Old Hand — Where the Letters Were Born
sections.seeker_text: The Seeker asked: Before you show me God's Name, I have to ask a question that sits underneath all the others. Letters didn't fall from the sky. Somewhere, somebody took the first picture and made it stand for a sound — and after him the whole world learned to write. Who was he? Where did he stand? And how did Israel come by her letters? Before we open the Name, I want to meet the hand that wrote it.
